output.answer: LinkedIn (Microsoft-owned) faces no single dominant head-to-head rival; its main competitors are platforms that compete for slices of its business: Indeed and ZipRecruiter (job boards/recruiting), Glassdoor and Fishbowl (employer reviews and industry talk), Xing (German-speaking professional networking), Alignable and Meetup (small-business and in-person networking), and general social platforms — Facebook, Reddit, Slack/Discord communities and X — used for professional networking and B2B reach. Microsoft's own 10-K defines LinkedIn's competition as online professional networks, recruiting/talent-management/HR services companies, job boards, learning and development providers, advertising outlets, and lead-generation/customer-intelligence providers. Emerging AI-first professional networks and startup-focused platforms (Wellfound/AngelList, Peerlist, Contra) are the newest threat, with commentators arguing AI matching could erode LinkedIn's professional social graph.
caveats: Microsoft's 10-K describes competitor categories but names no specific LinkedIn competitors, so the named-company list (Indeed, Xing, etc.) comes from secondary industry/blog sources, not Microsoft.
Several list sources are vendor or alternative-platform blogs (e.g. DOER promotes its own platform; snov.io sells sales tools), so their framing of who 'competes' with LinkedIn is opinionated.
Claims that AI-native platforms could displace LinkedIn are commentary, not established market-share fact; LinkedIn's ~1.2 billion members still dwarf all listed rivals.

passages.quote: LinkedIn faces competition from online professional networks; recruiting, talent management, and human resource services companies; job boards; companies that provide learning and development products and services; online and offline outlets that generate revenue from advertisers and marketers; and online and offline outlets for companies with lead generation and customer intelligence and insights.

Competitors have already sensed the opportunity. [Naukri](https://www.naukri.com/) dominates India’s job-tech market, [Xing](https://www.xing.com/) remains strong in Germany, [Jack and Jill](https://jackandjill.ai/) searches 10,000 new jobs every hour for you, and [Welcome to the Jungle](https://uk.welcometothejungle.com/) makes you swipe for your next role. Then there’s [Toptal](https://www.toptal.com/), [Upwork](https://www.upwork.com/), and [AngelList](https://angel.co/) cater to project-based and start-up talent. Each is experimenting with AI for matching, scoring, and verification. Regional clones will multiply as economies seek control over local workforce data. The next evolution pairs platforms with personal AI agents that handle introductions, contracts and reputation autonomously. Once agents communicate directly, platform loyalty disappears. Reputation, skill data, and behavioural history become portable. The question shifts from _where_ a profile lives to _which_ agent represents capability.

| Platform | Best for | Price | Feed and ads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mybzz | Founders who want introductions, not a feed | Free to join | No feed. One to one AI matching |
| Peerlist | People in tech showing real work | Free | Work feed, light |
| Wellfound | Startup jobs with salary and equity shown | Free for candidates | Job board, not a feed |
| Xing | Careers in Germany, Austria, Switzerland | Free, paid Premium | Feed, ads on free |
| Alignable | Local small business referrals, North America | Free, paid Premium | Feed, promoted content |
| Contra | Independents selling project work | Free, Pro USD 29 a month | Portfolio and marketplace |
| Fishbowl | Candid, semi anonymous industry talk | Free | Feed by industry bowl |
| Skool | Creators running a paid community | USD 9 plus 10% of sales, or USD 99 plus 2.9% | Community feed, no ads |
| DOER | Ambitious people: network, community, courses and selling in one place | Free forever. Pro USD 30, Premium USD 100. Zero commission | No ads, no vanity metrics, nobody pays to be seen first |

When it comes to thought leadership and great opportunities, professionals are missing out if they’re not on LinkedIn. It’s the world’s largest professional network with over [1.2 billion members in 200 countries](https://news.linkedin.com/about-us) and regions worldwide.

key_facts.fact: Per Microsoft's FY2026 10-K, LinkedIn faces competition from online professional networks; recruiting, talent management, and HR services companies; job boards; learning and development providers; advertising-supported outlets; and lead-generation/customer-intelligence providers.
Commonly cited LinkedIn competitors include Alignable, Facebook, Indeed, Glassdoor, Meetup, Xing, Quora, Reddit, Slack and ZipRecruiter.
Newer/alternative professional networks compared against LinkedIn in 2026 include Wellfound (formerly AngelList Talent), Peerlist, Xing, Alignable, Contra, Fishbowl (owned by Glassdoor) and Skool.

Regional and niche rivals named by City A.M.: Naukri (India job market), Xing (Germany), Jack and Jill, Welcome to the Jungle, Toptal, Upwork and AngelList, each experimenting with AI matching and verification.

Search Engine Journal lists professional-networking alternatives to LinkedIn as Meetup, Eventbrite Communities, Discord, Slack communities, Facebook Groups, Reddit, X (Twitter) and AngelList, noting LinkedIn remains the largest professional network with over 1.2 billion members.
